html:
The Illyrian Wars were three wars from 229 to 168 BCE in which the Roman Republic defeated the kingdom of the Illyrians on the coast of today's Albania and Montenegro.

The Illyrian queen Teuta let her people's ships raid Italian traders in the Adriatic, and when Roman envoys protested one was killed. Rome sent a fleet in 229 BCE, its first military venture across the Adriatic, and forced Teuta to give up the coast. In 168 BCE the last king, Gentius, was beaten at his capital of Scodra, today's Shkodër, in the same year Rome crushed Macedon. The region became the Roman province of Illyricum, crossed by the Via Egnatia. Albanians often see the Illyrians as their ancestors.
sum: The Illyrian Wars were three wars from 229 to 168 BCE in which the Roman Republic defeated the kingdom of the Illyrians on the coast of today's Albania and Montenegro.
